manifest.name: dsh-usage-ledger
manifest.description: DeepSeek Harness plugin: a local usage ledger for token consumption, cache hit rate and estimated cost, per day, per model and per workspace.
manifest.author: 白白酱 <cp990207@users.noreply.github.com> (https://github.com/cp990207)

bundle.text:
# Bundle defaults. Per-model prices live in the plugin's built-in catalog
# (index.js DEFAULT_PRICES) and are configurable at runtime via the ⚙ Prices
# button in the ledger, which writes a user profile patch row on save.
- insert:
    - id: usage-ledger
      name: 'dsh-usage-ledger'
      config:
        currency: USD

readme.text:
A local-first usage ledger for DeepSeek Harness: mines the session logs on this
machine and reports per-day / per-model / per-workspace token consumption,
cache hit rate, tool-vs-chat split, and an estimated cost.

本地用量账本插件：从本机会话日志统计每日 / 每模型 / 每工作区的 token 消耗、缓存命中率、工具请求占比，并按配置单价估算开销。

Install it as a DeepSeek Harness plugin from this repository — in the desktop
app open the plugin market (插件市场) install field and paste:

```
github:cp990207/dsh-usage-ledger
```

Or from a local clone, point the same field at the absolute path of the
checkout. The bundle patch registers the `usage-ledger` entry with the ledger
dashboard in the header; no extra configuration is needed.

When you install from a local directory by hand, keep the installed
`package.json` `name` equal to the specifier the profile loads (for example
`@local/usage-ledger`). The host validates that the icon resolved through
`<specifier>/icon` stays inside a package with that exact name; a mismatch only
surfaces as a "Plugin metadata … icon must remain inside its package directory"
diagnostic.

- Daily token & cost overview with today / 7d / 30d / all-time range filters
- Per-model table: requests, uncached input, cache read/write, output, hit rate, cost
- Share pies (tokens & cost), daily cost bar chart
- Workspace breakdown (sessions merged by cwd) and tool-call ranking
- **Instant startup after the first run**: folded sessions are cached on disk, so
  only logs that changed are re-read (see [Fold cache](#fold-cache))
- **Price configuration**: a ⚙ Prices button in the header opens a per-model
  price editor (input / output / cache read / cache write, per 1M tokens)

1. **Built-in catalog** — the plugin ships with USD list prices for the models
   it knows (Kimi, GLM, MiniMax, DeepSeek coding-plan models, verified against
   official pricing pages). Catalog prices follow plugin updates.
2. **Observed models** — model names come from your own session logs, so the
   editor always lists exactly the models you actually used.
3. **Custom overrides** — any row edited in the ⚙ dialog is persisted into your
   user profile patch (via the host's config editor) and takes precedence over
   the built-in catalog. Untouched rows keep following the catalog.
4. **Fallback** — models without any price are estimated at the `*` fallback
   row (default $0.50 in / $2.00 out per 1M tokens) and flagged in the UI.

Saving restates every historical day instantly: the plugin stores token totals
and derives cost at read time, so a price edit needs neither a refold nor a
cache rewrite.

A cold start replays every session log (decompressing the zstd JSONL and folding
each event), which takes seconds once a machine has a few hundred sessions and
is repeated on every plugin activation — including the reload that follows each
price save.

`index.js` therefore persists the fold to
`$DSH_HOME/cache/usage-ledger/fold-cache.json` (default `~/.dsh/cache/...`,
`DSH_HOME` respected). Each entry stores the folded token/request totals plus the
session log's persistence `revision` (`dev:ino:size:mtimeNs:ctimeNs`). On
activation the plugin takes one `sessionPersistence.list()` snapshot, adopts a
cached entry only when the revision still matches, and re-reads just the sessions
that changed. Live sessions are always refolded from the event stream.

The cache stores no cost, only measurable counters, so it is safe to delete: the
next activation simply folds everything again. Writes are atomic (temp file +
rename), coalesced, and skipped when nothing changed; a run writes the cache
once after its startup fold and once on shutdown, so serving the dashboard does
no extra I/O and a corrupt or partial file is ignored.

Serving is pure aggregation over the folded states: display metadata (model,
title, first prompt) is folded from the log's own events, so opening the panel
never re-reads a session log. In particular, titles come from `session/title`
events rather than `sessionQuery.readTitleSnapshots`, which would reload every
session corpus on each request.

The plugin's config is `{ currency: string, prices: Record<string, {input,
output, cacheRead, cacheWrite}> }`. Prefer the ⚙ dialog; hand-editing the
`usage-ledger` row of your profile's `cordis.patch.yml` works too:

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: usage-ledger
      name: 'dsh-usage-ledger'
      config:

If the host environment has no config editor, the ⚙ button is hidden and the
dashboard explains how to edit the patch instead.

All data is computed locally from session logs. The HTTP endpoint listens on
the loopback interface only and rejects cross-site requests.

The ⚙ Prices editor needs a host that mounts the `configEditor` service
(DeepSeek Harness desktop and web both do). On hosts without it the plugin
still folds the session log and serves the dashboard — read-only, priced from
the built-in catalog.
